Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

unanimously adverb

also with one voice, unanimous

classical

Cic. Att. 2.18.1: ūnā vōce omnium (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 180, 400, 399

ūnā vōce

with one voice

Other words

  • ūnanimus, ūnanima, ūnanimum — of one mind, unanimous

    declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Stich. 5.4.49: ūnanimī sumus (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Plaut., Catull., Stat.)

  • ūnanimis, ūnanime — unanimous

    declension · also used · post-classical · Claud. Cons. Prob. et Olybr. 231 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 399

    Lewis & Short calls this form post-classical; the classical adjective is ūnanimus.

Examples

  • omnibus sententiīs

    unanimously (by all the votes)Traupman 400

See also vote.

SourcesLewis & Short: vox

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 180.
